andrea: FYI saw a noticeable perf regression in the Mixtral MoE canary after the kernel v2.4 rollout — p95/p99 jumped on routing-heavy workloads. opening thread to triage. @samir @lee

andrea: Quick numbers from the canary (same traffic split, router-topk=64):
- before (kernel v2.3): p50=18ms p95=82ms p99=210ms
- after  (kernel v2.4): p50=19ms p95=110ms p99=380ms

andrea: Repro harness: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"https://canary.redwood/api/v1/generate?model=mixtral-moe&batch=8&len=64\"` with per-request trace header `x-rw-trace:1`. noticed spikes correlate with certain routing patterns.

samir: can you paste the flamegraph or perf top? is kernel selection flipping to a slow path?

andrea: pasted small perf dump (trimmed):
```
# pprof --text cpu.prof
flat  flat%   sum%        cum   cum%   samples name
0.32s  12.5% 12.5%   0.32s 12.5%  mixtral::kernel::moe_gemm_blocked
0.28s  10.9% 23.4%   1.90s 74.1%  mixtral::router::route_scatter
0.21s   8.2% 31.6%   2.11s 82.1%  cuda_kv_cache::evict_if_needed
```
link: https://gist.github.com/redwood-internal/abcdef (flame + raw pprof)

lee: interesting — my hunch: RoPE scaling change + v2.4 kernel heuristics = different GEMM kernel chosen for the MOE expert projection. that kernel has worse throughput for the small-ish per-expert batch sizes we get under topk=64, so you see latency tail blow up when router distribution is spiky. also KV eviction samples => cache pressure/fragmentation might be amplifying it.

lee: quick experiment ideas: force previous kernel for mixtral-moe, try router topk 64->32, and/or increase per-expert parallelism so GEMM sizes align better with the optimized kernel shapes. also try a higher kv_cache_capacity to avoid eviction thrash.

maria: ran a small A/B earlier on a lower scale: changed router.top_k=32 + expert_parallelism=2 on canary. results (same bench): p99 dropped ~12% vs current canary, p95 ~9% better. cost: tokens/expert went up ~5%. seems promising as a short-term mitigator.

andrea: thanks @maria, can you drop the exact config snippet?

maria: config snippet we tested:
```json
{
  \"model\": \"mixtral-moe\",
  \"router\": { \"top_k\": 32, \"router_temp\": 1.0 },
  \"runtime\": { \"expert_parallelism\": 2, \"kv_cache_capacity\": \"1.5x\" }
}
```

samir: another quick repro: run the microbench with env var to force the older kernel path: `INFER_KERNEL_WHITELIST=mixtral_v2_3 ./bench/microbench --model mixtral-moe --batch 8 --steps 200` — compare p99 across kernel variants + topk values. canary infra lets you toggle kernel selection via the per-model kernel map.

andrea: I ran microbench yesterday evening, results (median of 5 runs):
- topk=64, kernel v2.4: p99=385ms
- topk=64, kernel v2.3: p99=205ms
- topk=32, kernel v2.4: p99=295ms
- topk=32, kernel v2.3: p99=190ms
so forcing v2.3 buys most of the tail improvement, but lowering topk helps too.

andrea: conclusion: two contributing factors = (1) kernel selection heuristic in v2.4 picks a slower GEMM for our per-expert shapes, (2) KV cache eviction thrash widens the tail when routing is spiky.

lee: actionable plan:
- short-term: pin kernel v2.3 for mixtral-moe on canary and roll router.top_k=32 for 12h canary, watch p99/cost.
- mid-term: adjust kernel-selection heuristics to prefer the old kernel for small per-expert batch widths OR add a per-model kernel whitelist in the runtime.
- long-term: make router scheduling aware of kernel performance (heuristic: if chosen expert batch size < X, prefer lower-topk or increase parallelism) and add KV cache backpressure metrics to routing decisions.

samir: I'll open the runtime PR for per-model kernel whitelist + a feature flag `runtime.kernel_pinning` so ops can toggle without full rollback.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by @samir: runtime/pr-246-kernel-whitelist -> canary cluster (zone-a)

andrea: thanks folks. I'll monitor the canary and post a short follow-up after 6h. if canary looks good we'll roll to prod with the kernel pin and topk change. :thumbsup:
